chunks: And from him, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Isma'il ibn Marar, from Yunus, from Mufaddal ibn 'Amr, who said:

I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'We have young men and girls who are unable to fast due to the severity of the thirst that afflicts them.' He said: 'Let them drink the amount by which their souls are satisfied and which they fear [from causing harm/exhaustion].'
The Sheikh (may Allah have mercy on him) said: 'And none of those we mentioned may have marital relations, unless a great need drives them to do so.' That is indicated by what he narrated:
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for children or young people who cannot fast due to severe thirst or weakness?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* outlines the principle of *darura* (necessity) for the young and weak, permitting them to break their fast by drinking only what is required to stave off harm rather than full satiation. It further extends this concession to marital relations when necessary to prevent the distraction or harm of prolonged fasting, reflecting the Shia juristic emphasis on preserving health and spiritual focus over rigid ritual observance in cases of genuine weakness.
